structuralFindings.description: comp_build internal shape (variant-band annotations -> COMPONENT_SET -> y-axis legends -> build_description) held identically across all 10 comp_build instances.
comp_build_var_description grammar '{key} - {value}' repeated, joined by a dot-separator glyph, held identically across all 40 annotation bands.
en_dash text nodes contain a literal hyphen (U+002D), never a typographic en dash (U+2013), across all 80 occurrences.
The specific pairing {Center - Fill <-> Optional, Left - Hug <-> Leading/Trailing/Both} is the exact Layout/Symbol correlation observed in every one of the 10 Button component sets.

The general principle that declared VARIANT axes on a COMPONENT_SET may be correlated rather than independently combinable, and that naive Cartesian expansion can overstate the real design space, is a Figma-level phenomenon (not a Button API detail) but is only evidenced here via Buttons.

evidence.note: Not verified against any non-Button component in this file or elsewhere.

structuralFindings.description: Disabled-restricted component sets (State limited to one value) omit the x-axis legend row but retain build_description (headline + divider), for both of the 2 observed disabled sets.
Theme is implemented by binding the same variable to different container frames, which resolve to different mode-specific literal values, for both of the 2 observed theme containers in this file.

The general principle that Figma variable modes (rather than duplicate named styles) can implement theme switching is a file/Figma-level mechanism, not Button-specific, but is only evidenced here via the Buttons page's two theme containers.
The top-level page order (intro -> divider -> representation -> divider -> builds) occurs exactly once in this file (one component_box); it has not been observed to repeat, even within Buttons.

evidence.note: Classified 'unknown' for generalizability specifically because n=1 within this file; the shape itself is observed, its recurrence is not.

structuralFindings.description: The partition into exactly 3 semantic families (Primary/Secondary/Disabled) with hr dividers between them is specific to this one component_builds_section; the comp_build_section internal shape (headline + builds_container) does repeat 3/3 times.

Naming-convention violations exist and are not schema/lint-enforced: 4/38 var_col-title-role nodes are named 'Label' instead of 'var_col_title'; 4 comp_pan-role wrapper frames are named 'container'; the light-mode theme heading is named 'Subheading' vs. the dark-mode 'rep_title'; a capital-I typo ('Center - FIlled') ships in both theme panels.

evidence.note: Classification 'unknown' used deliberately: this finding describes an absence of enforcement, not a structural invariant, and the enum has no dedicated 'confirmed_inconsistency' value.

INSTANCE.variantProperties data therefore proves specific axis combinations exist as real components, but only for the combinations shown in the representation gallery, not for the matrix cells inside each COMPONENT_SET.

The v0.2.0-draft contract treated the get_screenshot(NODE-0557) result as component_children_verified-level evidence and claimed physical completeness for NODE-0313. That evidence level has been split (visual_matrix_verified vs. component_children_enumerated) and the screenshot correctly reclassified as visual_matrix_verified only, which does not meet the completeness bar. Net effect: 0 of 10 component sets now meet the bar (previously reported as 1 of 10). This finding exists purely for cross-version traceability.

structuralFindings.description: The v0.3.0-draft contract and validator claimed 5/5 enforceability but had five real enforcement gaps: fully_enumerated was label-based (an artifact could be fabricated/reused across sets); ownerConfirmations resolution was one-directional (an orphan confirmation record passed silently); layoutRepresentations[].allocation coverage only checked for zero coverage, not exactly-one, and its axis check unioned declared axes across referenced variants instead of requiring every one; the qualifying-evidence-levels policy field was unconstrained; and generate_tables.py had no drift-detection mode. All five are closed in v0.3.1-draft (CV-11 added; CV-3/CV-6/CV-7 corrected; CV-1 gained a schema-enforced floor restriction; generate_tables.py --check added). This finding exists purely for cross-version traceability.

validationRules.description: Naming drift with an unambiguous structural role.
validationRules.detectionCondition: A node's literal name differs from the conventional name for its structural role, but the role is still unambiguous from node type, position, and sibling context.
validationRules.action: Log the mismatch as a finding; continue processing using the structural role, not the literal name.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: No escalation required; include in the build's finding report for human awareness.

validationRules.detectionCondition: A node's name, type, and position are jointly insufficient to determine its structural role with confidence.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Escalate to human review before continuing; do not guess the role.

validationRules.description: Unresolved axis correlation must not gate a write.
validationRules.detectionCondition: A correlatedAxisTuples entry has approvalBasis == 'unresolved', and a downstream operation would use its proposedValidCombinations/observedCombinations to restrict or expand a variant matrix.
validationRules.action: Do not use this tuple to allocate a matrix or to gate any Figma write operation.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Escalate for owner confirmation (approvalBasis -> owner_confirmed) or structural enumeration (approvalBasis -> fully_enumerated) before use.

validationRules.description: A 'fully_enumerated' approval must be re-checked at use time, not just trusted from the contract.
validationRules.detectionCondition: A correlatedAxisTuples entry has approvalBasis == 'fully_enumerated' and a Builder is about to rely on its approvedCombinations for a write, without independently re-confirming that every relevant component set still shows component_children_enumerated coverage (data can go stale between contract authoring and Builder use).
validationRules.action: Re-verify coverage before trusting the approval; do not treat a past 'fully_enumerated' label as a standing guarantee.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: If re-verification fails or cannot be performed, escalate to human review before proceeding.

validationRules.description: Physical completeness claims require component-child-level evidence.
validationRules.detectionCondition: coveragePolicy.perComponentSetCoverage[i].physicalCompletenessClaimed=true while physicalCoverageEvidenceLevel is schema_only, observed_instances, or visual_matrix_verified.
validationRules.action: Reject the claim; downgrade physicalCompletenessClaimed to false.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Obtain component_children_enumerated evidence (a real structural descent/API listing of the COMPONENT_SET's children, not merely a screenshot) or owner_confirmed sign-off before re-claiming.

validationRules.description: Matrix allocation requires explicit human approval before use.
validationRules.detectionCondition: Any layoutRepresentations[].allocation[] entry's approvalStatus is not 'approved'.
validationRules.action: Do not generate or write any documentation matrix based on that allocation.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Route to a human reviewer for explicit approval with a resolvable ownerConfirmationRef; re-check status before any Figma write.

validationRules.description: Theme mode names must be read from the file, never assumed.
validationRules.detectionCondition: Any logic assumes theme mode names 'Dark'/'Light' (or any fixed pair) without reading themeModel.modes for the specific file being processed.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Re-derive theme handling from themeModel.modes for the specific file being processed.

validationRules.description: Canonical values and display-label captions must not be interchanged.
validationRules.detectionCondition: A caption string sourced from var_col_title, variant_value, or build_title is passed as the canonical property value to a Figma write operation.
validationRules.action: Block the write; substitute the canonical value from componentSets/propertySchemaVariants.

validationRules.description: Button-scoped findings must not be silently generalized to other components.
validationRules.detectionCondition: A structuralFindings entry with appliesToScopes=buttons or classification=button_specific_pattern is applied to a non-Button component without a corresponding candidate_cross_component_invariant or owner_declared_standard entry covering that same finding.
validationRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Re-scope the finding to owner_declared_standard only after explicit confirmation, or re-derive the rule for the new component from its own evidence.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Weak evidence must not be paired with a physical-completeness claim.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: physicalCompletenessClaimed==true while physicalCoverageEvidenceLevel is outside {component_children_enumerated, owner_confirmed}, or is absent from the declared qualifying set.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Downgrade the claim, or obtain the required evidence level.

contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: Two entries in the same array share an id. componentSets[].id must be unique; buildFrameId is a many-to-one REFERENCE and may repeat freely, but must never equal any componentSets id.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Assign a unique id; re-run the validator.

contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: familyId / schemaVariantId / coverage references do not resolve, or bidirectional membership disagrees.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Fix the reference on both sides.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Layout-representation and typed-scope reference integrity, and explicit representation of undocumented schema variants.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: A layoutRepresentations appliesTo / namingRuleRef, a typedScope scopeRef, a treatment propertyKey or a nonVariantPropertyCoverage key fails to resolve; OR a schema variant is covered by no representation and is not listed in undocumentedSchemaVariantIds.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Fix the reference, or declare the variant undocumented explicitly.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Incomplete or duplicate correlated-axis tuple entry.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: A combination's keys do not equal the tuple axes, a value is not canonical in every referenced variant, or two combinations are semantically duplicate.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Fix the combination or the tuple scope.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Owner approval without a resolvable, bidirectionally-agreeing confirmation record.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: Any owner-gated claim references a confirmation that does not resolve, or whose scopeType/scopeRef does not point back at the same object; or a confirmation is orphaned.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Add a real confirmation, or downgrade the claim.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Allocation dimension referencing something that does not exist or is out of scope.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: Dispatched on dimension kind: variant_property/fixed_filter must name a VARIANT property declared in EVERY referenced schema variant with canonical values; component_set_identity must reference real component sets inside the representation's appliesTo scope and real naming rules.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Correct the dimension or the representation scope.

contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: Non-empty approvedCombinations without owner confirmation, or with approvalBasis='fully_enumerated' but not equal to the intersection of enumerated combinations across all in-scope sets.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Obtain confirmation, or set approvedCombinations to the true intersection.

contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: contractVersion, readinessStatus, approvalStatus.overall, blockers and the contract-level owner confirmation do not all agree.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Enumeration evidence must be artifact-backed and internally consistent.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: status='enumerated' without a contained, existing, hash-matching, shape-valid artifact whose componentSetId/fileKey/enumerationMethodClass agree, whose capturedAt parses, whose componentIds are unique, and whose derived combinations and count exactly match the declaration.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Produce a real artifact, or downgrade to not_enumerated.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Matrix allocations must be RECOMPUTABLE from evidence, per source documentation block.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: allocationEvidence.status='verified' without a contained, existing, hash-matching, shape-valid artifact; OR zero observations; OR observations referencing out-of-scope sets; OR rows/columns/bands/fixedFilters recomputed per source block that differ from the declared allocation; OR parallel source blocks that do not derive the same semantic allocation.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Recapture the allocation evidence, or correct the declared allocation to match it.

contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: class='node_name_parse' backing physicalCompletenessClaimed=true without a resolvable corroborating owner confirmation; or class='owner_supplied' without both a resolvable confirmation and a rawCaptureRef artifact.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Re-capture via an API class, or obtain the corroborating confirmation.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Competing display-label mappings within one effective scope.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: Two canonicalValueDisplayLabelMap entries share an (axis, canonicalValue) pair AND the same relationship class with overlapping effective scopes (including the unscoped case); OR two entries for one (axis, canonicalValue) with overlapping scopes declare the same display surface with different labels. An editorial_mapping and a typo entry for the same value are complementary, not competing, and are preserved separately by design.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Scope the mappings disjointly, or reconcile the conflicting surface.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Corroboration must resolve to hashed external contracts.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: level='multi_component_corroborated' with no external contract; a corroborating entry naming the current contract; or an artifact that is missing, hash-mismatched, unparseable, or declares a different contractId.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Add a real, hashed external contract, or downgrade to single_component_observed.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Coverage metrics must be discriminated and non-duplicated.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: Two classified metrics of the same kind within one (component set, representation) scope, or a matrix_cells metric whose representationId does not resolve.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Migration provenance, legacy states and migration-review gate.
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: authoringMode='authored' with a migrationReportRef or any legacy_*/migrationReviewRequired state; OR authoringMode='migrated' without a resolvable hash-verified migration report (required even when zero legacy states remain); OR a report that fails to pin the source contract or the migration tool by hash; OR any mismatch in either direction between emitted unresolved states and reported ones; OR unresolved states coexisting with approvalStatus='approved', readinessStatus='ready_for_production', or a missing blocker of the matching blockerClass; OR a legacy state backing a completeness claim or an approved allocation.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Emit a complete migration report, or resolve the states.

contractIntegrityRules.description: Representation node bindings (the operational locator table).
contractIntegrityRules.detectionCondition: A binding whose layoutRepresentationRef does not resolve; a duplicate containerNodeId; a rootNodeId equal to its own containerNodeId; or a verified matrix allocation with a source documentation block that no binding covers.
contractIntegrityRules.recoveryOrEscalation: Add or correct the binding. evidenceNodeIds is provenance and must never be used as an operational locator.

knownLimitations: Only the terminal export self-reports validation statistics; basic-tree counts were independently recomputed, not self-reported, and both recomputations agree with each other and with the terminal export's self-report.

Reference-resolution validation (unresolved named styles, unresolved variables, duplicate IDs) is only possible from the terminal export, because the basic-tree export carries no style or variable data at all.

explicitVariableModes occurs 0 times anywhere in the terminal export. The theme-mode resolution mechanism is therefore unverified, not directly observed, despite the resolved-value difference itself being directly observed.

Physical coverage verification at the component_children_enumerated level exists for 0 of 10 component sets. NODE-0313 was screenshotted (visual_matrix_verified), which is a real but categorically different, weaker kind of evidence -- it does not establish structural completeness. This is a correction from the prior contract revision, which had treated the screenshot as sufficient for a physical-completeness claim.

The 8 previously-unrecorded buildFrameId values (all sets except NODE-0313 and the two Disabled sets, which were separately corrected/confirmed) were derived by the same script-based extraction method used to confirm the user-supplied corrections for NODE-0560 and NODE-0568, and were independently cross-checked by a separate review pass. High confidence, Buttons scope.

The screenshot evidence artifact for NODE-0313 (evidence/comp_build_750-2443_screenshot.png) was originally saved only to an ephemeral, session-scoped scratch directory outside the project; it has been copied into this project's evidence/ folder specifically so it remains durable and independently re-hashable rather than pointing at a path that could vanish.

No non-Button component has been analyzed in this file or elsewhere. Every candidate_cross_component_invariant classification in this contract is an unverified hypothesis pending a second component example, not a confirmed rule.

correlatedAxisTuples CAT-1 was derived by automatic pattern detection over this file's own annotation text and instance data (approvalBasis='unresolved'); it has not been owner-confirmed or structurally enumerated, and per CV-6/CV-8 must not be treated as approved for any Figma write.

Identical rule/finding id sets appearing across this contract and its companion markdown documents (SF-*, VR-*, CV-*, BLK-*) are necessary but not sufficient evidence of semantic consistency between the documents -- the CV/VR rule tables in the markdown docs are generated directly from this file's own description/detectionCondition/action text specifically to close that gap; other prose was not mechanically diffed and could still drift.

v0.3.0-draft's enforcement had five real gaps (see SF-15) despite claiming full enforceability; v0.3.1-draft closes them, but this is a reminder that a validator passing 0 violations is only as strong as the checks it actually runs -- absence of a rejection is not proof of correctness beyond what was specifically tested. The fixture suite (33 fixtures as of this revision) is the concrete evidence for what is and is not covered; it is not exhaustive for every micro-check within CV-11 (see the fixture table's own scoping note).
